{{Short description|Type of vector bundle}}
In mathematics, a '''Nori semistable vector bundle''' is a particular type of [[vector bundle (algebraic geometry)|vector bundle]] whose first definition has been first implicitly suggested by [[Madhav V. Nori]],<ref>{{cite journal | last = Nori | first = Madhav V. | title =On the Representations of the Fundamental Group | journal = Compositio Mathematica | volume = 33 | year = 1976 | issue = 1 | pages = 29–42 | mr = 417179 | url = http://www.numdam.org/item/CM_1976__33_1_29_0.pdf|zbl=0337.14016}}</ref><ref>{{cite book |doi=10.1017/CBO9780511627064 |last1=Szamuely |first1=Tamás  | title = Galois Groups and Fundamental Groups | publisher = Cambridge Studies in Advanced Mathematics | volume = 117 | year = 2009|isbn=9780521888509 }}</ref> as one of the main ingredients for the construction of the [[fundamental group scheme]]. The original definition given by Nori was obviously not called ''Nori semistable''. Also, Nori's definition was different from the one suggested nowadays.<ref name=":Dos">{{cite journal|arxiv=1809.06755 |doi=10.2748/tmj.20200727 |title=On the fundamental group schemes of certain quotient varieties |year=2021 |last1=Biswas |first1=Indranil |last2=Hai |first2=Phùng Hô |last3=Dos Santos |first3=João Pedro |journal=Tohoku Mathematical Journal |volume=73 |issue=4 |s2cid=54217282|pages=565–595 }}</ref> The [[Category (mathematics)|category]] of Nori semistable vector bundles contains the [[Tannakian formalism|Tannakian category]] of [[essentially finite vector bundle]]s, whose naturally associated group scheme is the [[fundamental group scheme]] <math>\pi_1(X,x)</math>.

==Definition==

Let <math>X</math> be a scheme over a field <math>k</math> and <math>V</math> a vector bundle on <math>X</math>. It is said that <math>V</math> is ''Nori semistable'' if for any smooth and proper curve <math>C</math> over <math>\bar k</math> and any morphism <math>j:C\to X</math> the pull back <math>j^*(V)</math> is [[Stable vector bundle|semistable]] of degree 0.<ref>{{cite book |doi=10.1007/978-3-540-38955-2|title=Hodge Cycles, Motives, and Shimura Varieties|first1=P. |last1=Deligne|author-link=Pierre Deligne|first2=J. S.|last2= Milne|author-link2=J. S. Milne |series=Lecture Notes in Mathematics |year=1982 |volume=900 |isbn=978-3-540-11174-0 |chapter=Tannakian Categories|chapter-url={{Google books|gW5rCQAAQBAJ|page=147|plainurl=yes}}}}</ref>

==Difference with Nori's original definition==
Nori semistable vector bundles were called by Nori ''semistable'' causing a lot of confusion with the already existing definition of semistable vector bundles. More importantly Nori simply said that the restriction of <math>V</math> to any curve in <math>X</math> had to be semistable of degree 0. Then for instance in positive characteristic a morphism <math>j</math> like the [[Frobenius morphism]] was not included in Nori's original definition. The importance of including it is that the above definition makes the category of Nori semistable vector bundles tannakian and the group scheme associated to it is the <math>S</math>-fundamental group scheme<ref name=":Langer">{{cite journal |doi=10.5802/aif.2667|title=On the <math>S</math>-fundamental group scheme |year=2011 |last1=Langer |first1=Adrian |journal=Annales de l'Institut Fourier |volume=61 |issue=5 |pages=2077–2119 |arxiv=0905.4600 |s2cid=53506862 }}</ref> <math>\pi^S(X,x)</math>. Instead, Nori's original definition didn't give rise to a Tannakian category but only to an [[abelian category]].
